Question 1

1.1 Define a Projection

For this lab we want to calculate distances between features, therefore we need a projection that preserves distance at the scale of CONUS. For this, we will use the North America Equidistant Conic:


Code
eqdc <- '+proj=eqdc +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs'





1.2 - Get USA state boundaries

In R, USA boundaries are stored in the AOI package. USA state boundaries can be accessed with aoi_get(state = ‘conus’). Make sure the data is in a projected coordinate system suitable for distance measurements at the national scale (eqdc)


Code
conus_states <- aoi_get(state = "conus")

conus_states_proj <- st_transform(conus_states, crs = eqdc)





1.3 - Get country boundaries for Mexico, the United States of America, and Canada

In R, country boundaries are stored in the AOI package. Country boundaries can be accessed with aoi_get(country = c(“MX”, “CA”, “USA”)). Make sure the data is in a projected coordinate system suitable for distance measurements at the national scale (eqdc)


Code
countries <- aoi_get(country = c("MX", "CA", "USA"))

countries_proj <- st_transform(countries, crs = eqdc)





1.4 - Get city locations from the CSV file

Download the appropriate (free) dataset into the data directory of this project. Once downloaded, read it into your working session. Convert the data.frame to a spatial object using st_as_sf and prescribing the coordinate variables and CRS. Finally, remove cities in states not wanted and make sure the data is in a projected coordinate system suitable for distance measurements at the national scale


Code
unzip("/Users/Avery/github/lab-10-csu/data/data.zip", exdir = "data/unzipped")
library(readr)
cities_data <- read_csv("/Users/Avery/github/lab-10-csu/data/unzipped/uscities.csv")


Rows: 31254 Columns: 17

Code
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_data, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cities_proj <- st_transform(cities_sf, crs = eqdc)

cities_conus <- st_filter(cities_proj, countries_proj)






Question 2

Here we will focus on calculating the distance of each USA city to (1) the national border (2) the nearest state border (3) the Mexican border and (4) the Canadian border. You will need to manipulate you existing spatial geometries to do this using either st_union or st_combine depending on the situation. In all cases, since we are after distances to borders, we will need to cast (st_cast) our MULTIPPOLYGON geometries to MULTILINESTRING geometries. To perform these distance calculations we will use st_distance()


Code
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)



Attaching package: 'flextable'


The following object is masked from 'package:purrr':

    compose




2.1 - Distance to USA Border (coastline or national) (km)


Code
usa_union <- st_union(conus_states_proj)
# Checking my work
plot(usa_union, col = "red")









Code
usa_border <- st_cast(usa_union, "MULTILINESTRING")
# Checking my work
plot(usa_border, col = "red")









Code
cities_conus = mutate(cities_conus,
                      dist_to_usa_border = st_distance(cities_conus, usa_border),
                      dist_to_usa_border = set_units(dist_to_usa_border, "km"),
                      dist_to_usa_border = drop_units(dist_to_usa_border))

invisible(cities_conus$dist_to_usa_border)

cities_far_from_border <- cities_conus |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(city, state_name, dist_to_usa_border) |>
  arrange(desc(dist_to_usa_border)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  flextable()
cities_far_from_border

Question 3

In this section we will focus on visualizing the distance data you calculated above. You will be using ggplot to make your maps, ggrepl to label significant features, and gghighlight to emphasize important criteria


Code
library(ggplot2)




3.1 Data

Show the 3 continents, CONUS outline, state boundaries, and 10 largest USA cities (by population) on a single map. Use geom_sf to plot your layers. Use lty to change the line type and size to change line width. Use ggrepel::geom_label_repel to label your cities


Code
top_10_usa_cities <- cities_conus |>
  arrange(desc(population)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = top_10_usa_cities, col = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top_10_usa_cities,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3) +
  ggthemes::theme_map()












3.2 City Distance from the Border

Create a map that colors USA cities by their distance from the national border. In addition, re-draw and label the 5 cities that are farthest from the border


Code
top_5_cities_from_border <- cities_conus |>
  arrange(desc(dist_to_usa_border)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, col = "black", size = 0.5, lty = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = cities_conus, aes(col = dist_to_usa_border), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Distance to National Border (km)") +
  geom_sf(data = top_5_cities_from_border, col = "red", size = 1) + 
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top_5_cities_from_border,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3) +
  ggthemes::theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")












3.3 City Distance from Nearest State

Create a map that colors USA cities by their distance from the nearest state border. In addition, re-draw and label the 5 cities that are farthest from any border


Code
top_5_cities_from_states <- cities_conus |>
  arrange(desc(dist_to_states)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) + 
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.5, lty = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = cities_conus, aes(color = dist_to_states), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Distance to State Border (km)") +
  geom_sf(data = top_5_cities_from_states, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top_5_cities_from_states,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3) +
  ggthemes::theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")












3.4 Equidistance boundary from Mexico and Canada

Use gghighlight to identify the cities that are equal distance from the Canadian AND Mexican border (plus or minus) 100 km. In addition, label the five (5) most populous cites in this zone. Hint: (create a new variable that finds the absolute difference between the distance to Mexico and the distance to Canada)


Code
cities_conus <- cities_conus |>
  mutate(abs_diff_ca_mx = abs(dist_to_canada - dist_to_mexico))
zone <- cities_conus |>
  filter(as.vector(abs_diff_ca_mx) <= 100)

top5_cities_in_zone <- zone |>
  arrange(desc(population)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.5, lty = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = cities_conus, aes(color = abs_diff_ca_mx), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  gghighlight(as.vector(abs_diff_ca_mx) <= 100) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Distance Difference (km)") +
  geom_sf(data = top5_cities_in_zone, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top5_cities_in_zone,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3) +
  ggthemes::theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

Question 4

Recently, Federal Agencies have claimed basic constitutional rights protected by the Fourth Amendment (protecting Americans from random and arbitrary stops and searches) do not apply fully at our borders. For example, federal authorities do not need a warrant or suspicion of wrongdoing to justify conducting what courts have called a “routine search,” such as searching luggage or a vehicle. Specifically, federal regulations give U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) authority to operate within 100 miles of any U.S. “external boundary”. Further information can be found at the ACLU article


4.1 Quantifing Border Zone

Report the following as a table: How many cities are in this 100 mile zone? (100 miles ~ 160 kilometers) How many people live in a city within 100 miles of the border? What percentage of the total population is in this zone? Does it match the ACLU estimate in the link above?


Code
cities_in_border_zone <- cities_conus |>
  filter(dist_to_usa_border <= 160)


Warning: Using one column matrices in `filter()` was deprecated in dplyr 1.1.0.
ℹ Please use one dimensional logical vectors instead.


Code
total_cities <- nrow(cities_conus)
total_pop <- sum(cities_conus$population)
zone_cities <- nrow(cities_in_border_zone)
zone_pop <- sum(cities_in_border_zone$population, na.rm = TRUE)

percentage <- zone_pop / total_pop * 100 

data.frame(
  'Total Cities' = total_cities,
  'Cities in Border Zone' = zone_cities,
  'Total Population' = total_pop,
  'Population in Border Zone' = zone_pop,
  'Percent of Population in Border Zone' = round(percentage)
) |>
  flextable()


Total.CitiesCities.in.Border.ZoneTotal.PopulationPopulation.in.Border.ZonePercent.of.Population.in.Border.Zone30,5949,502396,449,849214,172,22454


The article says about two-thirds of the US population lives within the 100 mile zone, which is around 66%. In comparison, in my calculation, I got that around 54% of the US population lives within the 100 mile zone.



4.2 Mapping Border Zone

Make a map highlighting the cites within the 100 mile zone using gghighlight. Use a color gradient from ‘orange’ to ‘darkred’. Label the 10 most populous cities in the Danger Zone


Code
top10_in_zone <- cities_in_border_zone |>
  arrange(desc(population)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.5, lty = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = cities_conus, aes(col = dist_to_usa_border), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  gghighlight(dist_to_usa_border <= 160) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred", name = "Population") +
  geom_sf(data = top10_in_zone, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top10_in_zone,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3) +
  ggthemes::theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

4.3 : Instead of labeling the 10 most populous cites, label the most populous city in each state within the Danger Zone


Code
most_pop_cities <- cities_in_border_zone |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  filter(population == max(population, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_proj, fill = "white", lty = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_proj, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.5, lty = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = cities_conus, aes(col = dist_to_usa_border), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  gghighlight(dist_to_usa_border <= 160) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred", name = "Population") +
  geom_sf(data = most_pop_cities, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = most_pop_cities,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = Inf) +
  ggthemes::theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
